text: Αὐτὸς ἤψει. Doctrina II Dorothei, ante medium: Μὴ, τὸ ἔψῃ τὸ καλῶς. Leg. Μὴ τὸ ἔψητο καλῶς. Non illud recte coctum fuerat. Scribi etiam posset, ἐψητὸν, res cocta.
anchorLine: πηρεσίας ἀνεχόμενος· αὐτὸς ἤψει (n), αὐτὸς ἔπλυ-
en: Autos hepsei [He himself boiled]. Dorotheus, Doctrine 2, before the middle: 'Μὴ, τὸ ἔψῃ τὸ καλῶς.' Read: 'Μὴ τὸ ἔψητο καλῶς' (lest what was boiled not be done well). What he had cooked had not been right. One could also write ἐψητόν, 'a cooked thing'.

text: Nactus sum ista in codice Regio 1026, f. 188: Ὅρος τῆς ἁγίας καὶ οἰκουμενικῆς τετάρτης συνόδου Πατέρων ἁγίων ἐν Χαλκηδόνι, οἷς ἦν ἀριθμὸς ἑπτὰ συνθέτους ἔχων δραμούσας εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἐννάδας. Hoc est: Definitio sanctæ et œcumenicæ quartæ synodi Patrum sanctorum apud Chalcedonem, quorum numerus septem compositos continebat in se recurrentes novenarios. Ex hac ergo opinione fuerunt Patres Chalcedonenses numero duntaxat 567.
anchorLine: τῶν σ', καὶ ἡ ἐν Καλχηδόνι ⁶⁸ χλ' (ο). Καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ
en: I found this in the Royal codex 1026, fol. 188: 'Definition of the holy and ecumenical fourth synod of the holy Fathers at Chalcedon, whose number, containing seven composite (numbers), ran into itself nines.' That is: the definition of the holy and ecumenical fourth synod of the holy Fathers at Chalcedon, whose number contained within itself seven compound recurring novenaries. From this opinion, therefore, the Fathers of Chalcedon were only 567 in number.

text: Βρεκτά. Ordo monasterii Casulorum laudatus per Allatium, De missa præsanctificatorum, n. 7: Ἐσθίομεν ἄρτον, καὶ φάβα βρεκτόν. Comedimus panem, et fabam aqua maceratam. Moschi nostri, cap. 163, Ἄρτον καὶ βρεκτά· interpres, panem et cicer infusum; e mss. Καὶ ἐρεβίνθια βρεκτά.
anchorLine: κτὰ (p), ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον· καὶ τῷ νέῳ διὰ τῆς
en: Brekta [soaked things]. The rule of the monastery of the Casuli, cited by Allatius, De missa praesanctificatorum, n. 7: 'We eat bread and soaked beans' (Latin: we eat bread and beans macerated in water). In our Moschus, chap. 163: 'Bread and brekta'; the translator renders it bread and soaked chickpea; from the manuscripts: 'and soaked chickpeas, brekta'.

anchorLine: ἐσκεύαζεν τὴν κανδη-|λαν (r), καὶ ἧπτεν ὡς εἶχεν συνήθειαν, καὶ πρὸς
en: Kandelan [lamp]. To the Glossary of Johannes Meursius add the word kandelarios (lamp-keeper), from Theodore the Studite's Catecheses in the Escorial Library, where catechesis 2 of book I reads: 'On the care of the canonarch, the lamp-keeper, and the infirmarian.'

text: Σημειογράφου. Invenies in Lexicis, ut et σημειογραφεῖν. At σημειογραφεῖον non invenies, quod legitur pag. paulo ante citata Hodegi Anastasiani, statim post verba relata: Συγκαθεζομένων ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ σημειογραφείῳ τοῦ Καισαρίου. Apud Allatium, De perpetua consensione, etc., col. 674: Ἀπὸ τῶν σιγνογραφίων. Theodorus Studita, De sancto Platone, n. 16: Ἐσυρμαιογράφησεν. Ἐσπουδαιογράφησεν; Aristeas, χρυσογραφία; Syncellus, βίβλοι κεχρυσογραφημέναι.
anchorLine: σημειογράφου (s) τελείως, καὶ παρὰ τοῦ γραμματι-
en: Semeiographou [of the notary]. You will find this in the Lexicons, as also semeiographein. But semeiographeion you will not find, though it is read on the page cited a little earlier from the Hodegos of Anastasius, right after the words quoted: 'While we were sitting together in the notary's office of Caesarius.' In Allatius, On the Perpetual Agreement, etc., col. 674: 'From the signographia.' Theodore the Studite, On Saint Plato, n. 16: 'He wrote ...' 'He wrote with zeal'; Aristeas, 'gold-writing'; Syncellus, 'books written in gold.'
